summary: The note profiles five nutritional education programs launched in Charlotte between September 2023 and January 2024. They target families, schoolchildren, food-desert neighborhoods, people interested in mindful eating, and seniors. Together they aim to build healthier eating habits through workshops, cooking classes, gardening, and community participation.
one_line: Five Charlotte nutrition education programs launched September 2023 to January 2024 teach healthy eating to families, students, urban communities, mindful eaters, and seniors.
key_facts: The Family Table launched on September 15, 2023, through Charlotte Community Health Clinic (CCHC), led by Dr. Angela Simmons, with monthly workshops on meal planning and preparation for busy families.
The Family Table participants learn to read labels, select seasonal produce, budget for balanced nutrition, and attend family-friendly cooking classes.
Nutrition Notes was launched on October 3, 2023, by Charlotte-Mecklenburg School District to integrate nutrition education into the regular school curriculum.

Registered dietitian Teresa Yu of the district's Food Service Management team devised the Nutrition Notes curriculum for kindergarten through 12th grade, covering food groups, dangers of processed foods, and balanced plates.
Nutrition Notes uses garden-based learning, where students tend school gardens and use the harvested produce to learn plant biology and nutrition.
Urban Edible launched on November 1, 2023, under urban farmer and nutritionist Carlos Mendez, transforming unused urban spaces into vegetable gardens.
Urban Edible targets food deserts in Charlotte, offering fresh produce access and workshops on urban farming techniques and nutritional literacy.
Mindful Meals launched on December 5, 2023, conceived by holistic nutritionist Emily Parker, combining mindful eating practices with nutritional knowledge.
Mindful Meals workshops teach participants to listen to their bodies, take slow bites, and be present during meals, and cover macronutrients, meal timing, and psychological aspects of eating.
The Senior Nutrition Series launched on January 18, 2024, spearheaded by nutritionist Lucy Goldman, as workshops and social gatherings for Charlotte seniors.
The Senior Nutrition Series covers bone health, metabolism, and memory-boosting foods, and aims to help seniors stay independent and healthy.
The note says the programs' success depends on community participation and enthusiasm.
